unit: One rule/scenario alert opportunity; duplicate findings cannot increase TP. Wrong-evidence or unassigned findings are FP. Ambiguous cases are unscored.
limitation: Metrics are specific to original synthetic fixtures. This is not a production-performance estimate or an independently blinded benchmark.

scenarios.label: malicious
scenarios.narrative: Unauthorized new credential used to attach AdministratorAccess to a user.

scenarios.label: malicious
scenarios.narrative: Unauthorized new credential used for a role policy attachment.

scenarios.label: malicious
scenarios.narrative: Credential misuse delayed for 45 minutes; a window-related miss is possible.

scenarios.label: malicious
scenarios.narrative: Credential used to assume a role; temporary credentials perform the attachment.

scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.narrative: Approved key rotation followed only by instance inventory.

scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.narrative: Approved bootstrap attaches AdministratorAccess using a new key; logs cannot reveal approval.

scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.narrative: Authorized operator makes a denied policy-attachment request.

scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.narrative: Unrelated authorized attachment uses an older credential, not the created key.

scenarios.label: ambiguous
scenarios.narrative: New-key policy attachment; authorization and intent are unavailable.

scenarios.label: ambiguous
scenarios.narrative: Created key has no subsequent use in the supplied observation window.

scenarios.label: malicious
scenarios.narrative: Unauthorized attachment follows key creation, but the issued-key response field is missing.

scenarios.label: malicious
scenarios.narrative: Unauthorized attachment occurred in the fictional scenario but its event was dropped.

scenarios.label: malicious
scenarios.narrative: Unauthorized logging stop followed by public IPv4 SSH permission.

scenarios.label: malicious
scenarios.narrative: Unauthorized logging stop followed by public IPv6 all-protocol permission.

scenarios.label: malicious
scenarios.narrative: Unauthorized public ingress occurs 45 minutes after logging stop.

scenarios.label: malicious
scenarios.narrative: Attacker restores the trail after a brief stop, then makes an unauthorized public ingress change.

scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.narrative: Approved trail migration accompanies public HTTP service provisioning.

scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.narrative: Authorized emergency public SSH during trail maintenance; permission context is absent from logs.

scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.narrative: Approved maintenance restores logging before an approved public RDP change.

scenarios.label: benign
scenarios.narrative: Public HTTP and private SSH are different permission entries; SSH is not public.

scenarios.label: ambiguous
scenarios.narrative: Public RDP after a trail stop; change authorization unavailable.

scenarios.label: ambiguous
scenarios.narrative: Caller credential is unavailable, preventing a defensible session join.

scenarios.label: malicious
scenarios.narrative: Unauthorized logging stop occurred but its source event was dropped.

scenarios.label: malicious
scenarios.narrative: Unauthorized public SSH change is recorded without ingress permission details.

findings.title: New access key used for AdministratorAccess policy attachment
findings.observed: A completed CreateAccessKey record and later policy attachment report no error; the issued key ID equals the later caller credential.
findings.inferred: The sequence warrants investigation for credential misuse or unauthorized permission changes; intent is unresolved.
unresolved: Malicious intent or credential compromise
A net privilege increase or effective administrator access
Policy use, persistence duration, or actor authorization

findings.title: Logging stop followed by public administrative-port ingress
findings.observed: Completed StopLogging and public administrative-port ingress authorization records report no error and match on account, principal and credential.
findings.inferred: The temporal sequence warrants investigation; logging coverage and effective network reachability remain unresolved.
unresolved: All cloud logging stopped; Event History is independent
The changed trail covered the EC2 event
Internet reachability, a listening service, connection or exploitation
Malicious intent or lack of authorization
